digest.component_or_area: tickets-store reconciler and bridge state management
propositions: The committed .bridge_state cache grows uncontrollably (92% of 1.04 GiB) due to frequent churn in fields like baseline_advanced_at and last_get_pass that are not read by reconciliation logic

Eliminating the baseline_advanced_at timestamp field and moving last_get_pass to a separate .bridge_state/get_rotation.json file reduces marginal packed cost per version from 12.79 KB to approximately 1.74 KB (7.4x improvement)

A one-time git fast-export/filter/fast-import history rewrite removes historical .bridge_state mutations while preserving all commits and the byte-identical current HEAD tree, reducing the tickets branch from 1.04 GiB to ~98 MB
The reconciler must retain .bridge_state on-branch because it runs on ephemeral GitHub-hosted runners and requires durable git-backed state

Post-reclaim rollback is operator-controlled and fail-closed: stale-epoch clones abort at both sync._union_merge and push.py without merging, and writers must be re-cloned to recognize the epoch change

Rollout gates are evidence-based (descendant workflow execution, explicit host refresh, mixed-version self-healing proofs) rather than fixed-delay timers, with quiesced publication requiring zero active sessions, stopped rebar-mcp servers, and verified off-repo backup bundle
